newsitem.title: UK: RTZ Utah copper workers on strike.
newsitem.headline: RTZ Utah copper workers on strike.

text.p: Workers at Kennecott Corp's copper smelter in Utah went on strike on Wednesday but output was continuing, the firm's parent RTZ Corp Plc said.
About 1,800 unionised workers at the plant, which has been dogged by production problems since it went on stream in April 1995, have been working without a contract since September 30.
"Kennecott was informed by its unionised workers yesterday that the union workforce was on strike," John Hughes, head of public affairs for mining conglomerate RTZ Corp, told Reuters.
About 400 non-union employees work at the operation.
When asked if the firm was putting into force a plan to keep the $1 billion plant running, Hughes responded, "That is my understanding and they are continuing to produce copper."

It was unclear at what level production would continue at the smelter, which was designed to produce 310,000 short tons per year, but has been running at less than maximum levels after suffering from operation problems.

Kennecott President Bruce Farmer said in Salt Lake City earlier this week the smelter was currently operating at about 75 percent of capacity and would reach full capacity in the first quarter of next year.
This is about a year later than originally expected.
Another official of Kennecott Corp said on Wednesday operations would have to be curtailed in the event of a strike.
The convertor furnace was shut last autumn due to an explosion caused by water leaking onto hot metal.
Shares in RTZ, the British arm of mining giant RTZ-CRA dropped 12 pence to 972-1/2 pence on the news, but analysts did not see a major threat to results.
Three month copper prices on the London Metal Exchange bounced from an overnight low of $1,900 per tonne, augmented by the strike news, touching $1,930.
But the market, which had been following the situation in Utah, failed to jump out of its current $1,900-$1,970 range.
Hughes said he did not know whether any further negotiations were planned between the United Steelworkers of America union and the firm, which re-opened talks on Tuesday.
The talks had focused on wage and pension issues, Kennecott officials in Utah have said. The firm had been looking for a three-year contract containing a no-strike clause.
